exposure: International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) CTG classification
Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) CTG classification
National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) CTG classification
5-tier system by Parer and Ikeda CTG classification
outcome: Neonatal acidemia at birth (umbilical artery pH<7.00)
cohort: The study included 86 singleton pregnancies (43 with umbilical artery pH<7.00 and 43 with pH>=7.00) with cephalic presentation, admitted during the active phase of first stage of labour, and gestational age 37+0 to 41+6 weeks, excluding those with specific high-risk conditions.
finding: The 5-tier classification system proposed by Parer and Ikeda for assessing CTG in labour demonstrated superior predictive value for severe neonatal acidemia at birth compared to FIGO, RCOG, and NICHD intrapartum CTG classifications.
